analysis:
This batch contains only documentation: changelog.d/deadline-admission-estimators.md (new, lines 1-6) and docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (new section "Deadline admission rates" at head ~549-580, plus a code-map row at ~634). No executable source is in the supplied evidence, so the described estimator changes in AdmissionRateEstimators.swift, EngineV2Bridge+Admission.swift and the MTP policy code were not reviewed.

Security-relevant claims in the docs: (1) first-token deadline admission is a time check only; it changes no KV grant, load quotation, activation floor, serving width or memory concurrency, and admitted requests still pass slot and process byte admission. This is consistent with the existing memory-model invariants and with T-010 and T-029 (availability). (2) A new env var, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES=0, restores the old estimators, and `darkbloom start` forwards it to the launchd-managed provider. This is an operator-local rollback knob. It affects only local admission timing, not authentication, attestation, encryption or data exposure, and it does not touch TB-002, TB-009 or TB-011. (3) Admission now floors the prefill rate at 1/8 of the idle startup calibration and treats stale isolated evidence as absent after 30 minutes on an idle Mac. The change is aimed at availability: it avoids a lockout after one slow sample. The residual risk is a more permissive admission on a degraded Mac. Whether that lets requests through that then miss deadlines or consume GPU (T-010, T-029) depends on code outside this batch.

All of that is unverified. Integration or a later pass should confirm the following in the actual Swift code: the idle gating, which must cover other resident models, loads, encoder preparation and cache transfers; the posture check; that no coordinator-visible capacity wire fields change (the docs say they do not); and that the env override cannot be set by a remote party. Nothing in the docs introduces a new trust boundary crossing, secret handling, or consumer-controlled input into the estimators. The prefix-cache TTFT oracle (T-041) is unaffected by documented behavior, though timing-derived admission inputs could in principle interact with it. This is not evidenced here.
